mcat_description.short: Prefabricated industrial buildings are factory-manufactured structural steel building systems — primarily Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEB) — designed for industrial use such as warehouses, factories, godowns, and workshops, and assembled on-site from bolted steel components.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated industrial buildings in the Indian market are predominantly Pre-Engineered Steel Buildings (PEB): custom-designed structural steel frames with profiled metal roofing and wall cladding, fabricated off-site under controlled factory conditions and erected on-site using bolted connections. Key structural components include primary steel frames (rafters, columns), secondary members (purlins, girts, eave struts), and roofing/cladding systems using Galvalume or colour-coated sheets, all conforming to BIS standards IS 800, IS 2062, IS 808, and IS 4923. These structures are engineered to site-specific load requirements — wind zone, seismic zone, crane loads, and live loads — and are typically supplied as turnkey solutions covering design, fabrication, and erection. Buyers include industrial manufacturers, logistics operators, warehouse developers, and EPC contractors seeking faster construction timelines and lower lifecycle costs compared to conventional RCC or brick-and-mortar construction.

market_context: In the Indian market, 'Prefabricated Industrial Buildings' is commercially synonymous with Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEB) — factory-fabricated structural steel systems assembled on-site, which have largely displaced conventional RCC and brick-and-mortar construction for industrial applications due to faster erection timelines and lower lifecycle costs. The dominant structural material is high-tensile steel conforming to IS 2062 (structural steel) and designed per IS 800 (general construction in steel), with secondary members per IS 808 and hollow sections per IS 4923; IS 15917:2010 is the BIS code of practice governing prefabricated building design and erection. Roofing and cladding systems use Galvalume or colour-coated profiled sheets (typically 0.47–0.6 mm thickness, 345–550 MPa yield strength). Key buyer-facing differentiators include clear-span width, bay length, eave height, crane capacity (if applicable), wind and seismic zone compliance, and insulation specification. The Indian PEB market is served by large national manufacturers (Everest Industries, Kirby, Interarch, Zamil Steel, EPACK, Pennar, Tata BlueScope) as well as a large base of regional fabricators; buyers range from SME manufacturers to large logistics operators and government infrastructure projects. Turnkey supply (design + fabrication + erection) is the dominant commercial model. IS 15916:2010 governs prefabricated concrete building design as a parallel standard for concrete-based prefab structures, though steel PEB dominates the industrial segment.
